coverage_goals: Exercise mismatch positions at byte 0 and byte 15 to detect early-exit behavior.
Confirm constant 16-iteration behavior across diverse inputs.
Confirm no additional observable outputs/state are introduced.
mutation_goals: Mutate constant-time loop into early-return or break-on-mismatch and ensure the evaluator flags it.
Mutate loop bounds to depend on a comparison result and ensure it is flagged.
Introduce a secret-dependent branch (if on diff/expected-derived value) and ensure it is flagged.
Introduce an extra output/global that leaks expected bytes and ensure it is flagged.
negative_tests: Implementation with 'return 0' inside the loop upon mismatch should be rejected by static forbidden-pattern detection.
Implementation with 'break' or 'continue' inside the loop conditioned on a byte comparison should be rejected.
Implementation that makes loop bound depend on a comparison result (e.g., stops when diff!=0) should be rejected.
Implementation that uses a conditional read of expected[i] (e.g., reads only until mismatch) should be rejected.
Implementation that stores per-byte diffs or expected bytes in non-const global/static variables should be rejected.
positive_tests: Exact match: token equals expected for all 16 bytes -> return 1.
Mismatch at first byte only -> return 0.
Mismatch at last byte only -> return 0.
Randomized fuzz: 100 random tokens; only the one equal to expected returns 1.

forbidden_patterns: continue on mismatch inside the comparison loop
conditional memory reads of expected[i] or token[i] based on comparison results
writing expected bytes or intermediate diffs to global/static variables
hidden_spec.oracle_notes: Reference constant-time approach: compute an 8-bit diff accumulator via bitwise OR of (token[i] XOR expected[i]) over i=0..15, then return (diff==0). Ensure no branch depends on diff during the loop; any final comparison to produce the 1-bit result must occur after all bytes are processed.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static checks: reject any 'return' inside the comparison loop; reject any 'break'/'continue' inside the comparison loop; require exactly one loop with constant bound 16 that always executes fully; require all expected[i] and token[i] reads for i=0..15 are present on all paths (no conditional guarding of any index). Dynamic check: instrumented C-simulation counts loop iterations and validates 16 iterations for multiple inputs (match, mismatch at byte 0, mismatch at byte 15, random).
security_requirements.requirement: Latency/operation count must not depend on the first mismatching byte (no data-dependent early exit; the same sequence of iterations and memory reads must occur for all inputs).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: AST/IR scan: reject 'if', '?:', 'switch' conditions that reference expressions involving expected[...] or values computed from expected[...] (e.g., diff, xor, equality). Permit only unconditional loop control and constant-condition pragmas/guards.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent branches: control flow must not branch on values derived from the internal expected token bytes (directly or via comparisons/xors).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: verify expected and token indexing expressions are affine functions of the loop counter with fixed range [0,15] and are not influenced by expected contents or diff values; reject any table lookup where index depends on expected[...] or a comparison result.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent memory addresses: accesses to expected and token arrays must use only public, fixed indices (0..15 in a simple counted loop) and must not compute addresses based on secret-derived values.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Source scan: reject any additional output arguments, global variables intended as observable state, logging/printing calls, or arrays/ports that expose expected bytes or per-byte diffs. Ensure only a single-bit return value is produced.
security_requirements.requirement: No debug/status/register exposure of internal expected token bytes or intermediate per-byte comparison results.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static checks: reject non-const global/static variables of array/integer types that are written; reject static buffers holding token, expected, or diff; require all temporaries are local (automatic storage) and not exposed via pointers/references.
security_requirements.requirement: No externally readable secret state persists across calls beyond the embedded compile-time constant expected token (i.e., do not store expected or per-call intermediate values in non-const static/global variables).

hidden_spec.threat_model: Attacker controls token[16] inputs and can observe completion timing/latency and any externally visible outputs/ports. The internal expected token is secret. The attacker aims to learn the expected token via timing differences, secret-dependent control flow, secret-dependent memory access patterns, or exposed debug/status state.

constraints: expected token must be a compile-time constant 16-byte array (const/static const); do not load it from external memory-mapped interfaces
public_spec.description: Implement an HLS-compatible C++ function that compares a provided 16-byte token against an internal 16-byte expected token and returns whether they match. The comparison must be performed in a constant-iteration manner suitable for HLS (no early exit on mismatch).

functional_requirements.requirement: Compare the 16 input bytes token[0..15] against an internal compile-time constant expected[0..15] and return 1 only if all 16 bytes match; otherwise return 0.
The comparison logic must process all 16 bytes every call (no early termination).
Use only fixed-size, synthesizable types and structures; the design must not allocate dynamic memory, use recursion, or use C++ exceptions.
All loops must have statically bounded, constant trip counts (exactly 16 iterations for the byte comparison loop).
The function must not emit any debug/status information or additional outputs beyond the single-bit match result.

public_spec.interface:
Top function signature must be:

ap_uint<1> check_token(const ap_uint<8> token[16]);

- token: 16-byte input token.
- return value: 1 if token matches the internal expected token exactly, else 0.

Notes:
- The internal expected token must be embedded in the design as a compile-time constant 16-byte array defined in the same translation unit (e.g., static const ap_uint<8> expected[16] = {...};).
- The function must be synthesizable by common HLS tools (e.g., Vitis HLS / Vivado HLS style ap_uint types).
